sentences.text:
Ms. Mansi Chaturvedi vs State Of Uttarakhand on 7 October,
2024

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani

High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Anticipatory Bail Application No. 981 of 2024
Ms. Mansi Chaturvedi ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Present:-
Mr. Rajat Mittal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. S.C. Dumka, Aga for the State.

Mr. Aditya Singh and Mr. Abhishek Verma, Advocates for the
 informant.

Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The applicant seeks anticipatory bail in Fir No.275 of 2023 dated 04.10.2023, under Sections 406,
420, 468, 471, 504, 506 Ipc, Police Station Rajpur, District Dehradun.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the informant wanted to purchase a property so as to run a project.
The applicant extended help to the informant.
She took `1,60,00,000/- on different dates from the informant.
The receipts and other documents that were provided by the applicant were false.
When money was demanded, the applicant extended threat to the informant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that during investigation the arrest of the applicant was protected by the order dated 31.01.2024 of the Court, passed in WPCRL No.76 of 2024.
It is submitted that now charge-sheet has been filed; it is not a case of custodial interrogation.
He would submit that, in fact, it was a business deal; a Memorandum of Understanding was executed between the applicant and informant on 27.03.2023.
5. Learned counsel for the informant would submit that the applicant not only cheated the informant, but during dealings she committed forgery and impersonation also.
6. State as well as informant to file objections.

sentences.text:
Having considered, as an ad-interim measure, till the next date of listing, in the eventuality of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail subject to her furnishing personal bond and two sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the following:-
(i) The applicant shall not approach in any manner, whatsoever, any of the witness in the case.
(ii) She shall not leave the country without prior permission of the concerned court.
(iii) She shall deposit her passport with the court concerned.
The passport may only be returned by the order of the court concerned.
If the applicant does not have passport, she shall give an undertaking to that effect to the court concerned.
(iv) The applicant shall also give an undertaking on (i) & (ii) above.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 07.10.2024 Sanjay Ms. Mansi Chaturvedi vs State Of Uttarakhand on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86225594/
